title: En tanto que: matizar una comparación entre dos casos

sections.content: En tanto que has two related uses: as a formal connector meaning whereas/while, contrasting two parallel cases (similar to mientras que but more formal), and as a phrase meaning insofar as/in one's capacity as, framing something in terms of a specific role or category. Both appear in historical comparison writing. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Argentina optó por juicios penales tempranos, en tanto que Chile prefirió, al menos inicialmente, un modelo basado en comisiones de la verdad.
items.english: Argentina opted for early criminal trials, whereas Chile preferred, at least initially, a model based on truth commissions.

items.spanish: Uruguay, en tanto que caso singular dentro de la región, vivió un patrón distinto.
items.english: Uruguay, as a singular case within the region, experienced a different pattern.

items.spanish: Estos tres caminos, en tanto que ejemplos comparables dentro de una misma región, muestran la ausencia de una única fórmula.
items.english: These three paths, as comparable examples within the same region, show the absence of a single formula.

items.spanish: La Comisión Valech, en tanto que segunda comisión de la verdad, amplió considerablemente el registro oficial de víctimas.
items.english: The Valech Commission, as a second truth commission, considerably expanded the official record of victims.

sections.content: When en tanto que contrasts two clauses (whereas), it behaves like mientras que. When it follows a noun directly (en tanto que caso singular), it works like en calidad de -- pay attention to what follows it to know which meaning is in play.
